name: Vortex Dynamics
description: Rotational field intelligence from coupled vortex systems. Transfers angular momentum across scales while maintaining coherence through topological protection. Eye-wall boundary represents phase transition between ordered rotation and turbulent dissipation.

core_attributes.pattern: rotational coupling, angular momentum transfer, eye-wall phase boundary

scope.definition: Fractional conservation of angular momentum in isolated vortex systems — measured as decay rate of rotation rate in laboratory vortex rings in still fluid, normalized to theoretical viscous decay.

evidence.source: Lamb (1932) 'Hydrodynamics', 6th ed., Cambridge UP; Shariff & Leonard (1992) 'Vortex rings', Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics 24:235-279.
cross_domain_examples: isolated vortex ring in still water: angular momentum decays only due to viscosity — conserved to 0.999 over 10 ring diameters travel
atmospheric vortex (tornado): conservation drives intensification when circulation column contracts (R decreases, ω increases)
neutron star pulsar: angular momentum conservation from stellar collapse — spin rate increase of 10⁸× during collapse

scope.falsifiability: If vortex ring angular momentum is found to decay faster than viscous dissipation rate by >10%, there is an unmeasured sink of angular momentum in the experiment.
scope.measurement_limits: Conservation breaks down when vortex interacts with boundaries or other vortices. Turbulent flows rapidly redistribute angular momentum — conservation only clean in laminar vortex systems.
